question: What is the main goal of Primary Health Care (PHC) in a community?

options.A: Providing universally accessible and affordable essential health services
options.B: Focusing exclusively on surgical interventions for chronic illnesses
options.C: Building specialized tertiary hospitals in every local government area
options.D: Training only high-level medical consultants for village clinics

explanation: Think of PHC as bringing basic, affordable health care right to the doorsteps of the people who need it most. You've got this! [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why is Primary Health Care called the first point of contact in a health system?

options.A: It operates only inside large national teaching hospitals
options.B: It is where individuals and families first seek guidance and basic care
options.C: It exclusively handles complex surgical procedures and intensive care
options.D: It requires a referral letter from a specialist before a patient can visit

explanation: PHC is the open front door of healthcare where community members go first for everyday health needs and routine checkups. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h1)

question: In which year was the historic Alma-Ata Declaration on Primary Health Care held?
explanation: The landmark international conference that shaped modern community nursing took place in Alma-Ata in 1978. Great to keep in mind for your exams! [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h2)

question: What major global health target was famously set by the Alma-Ata Declaration?

options.A: Eradication of all infectious diseases by 1985
options.B: Health for All by the Year 2000
options.C: Privatization of all national health sectors
options.D: Free tertiary hospital care for every global citizen

explanation: Alma-Ata made history by rallying the world around the bold dream of 'Health for All by the Year 2000' through primary care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which PHC principle ensures that rural and underserved populations get a fair share of health services?
explanation: Equitable distribution simply means fairness—making sure health resources reach everyone, especially vulnerable groups who need them most. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h3)

question: A local health clinic invites village leaders and women's groups to help plan a new malaria campaign. Which PHC principle is this?
explanation: When locals help plan their own health programs, it's true community participation in action. Healthcare works best when people are involved! [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is a key component of Primary Health Care from the Alma-Ata Declaration?

options.A: Provision of safe water and basic sanitation

explanation: Clean water and basic sanitation are absolute foundation stones for preventing diseases in any community. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why is routine immunization considered a vital part of Primary Health Care?

options.A: It serves as a primary surgical cure for congenital heart defects
options.B: It is used exclusively to treat chronic lifestyle diseases in adults
options.C: It replaces the need for proper nutrition and clean drinking water
options.D: It actively prevents children from contracting dangerous, vaccine-preventable infectious diseases

explanation: Immunization is a powerful shield that stops deadly childhood infections before they can spread. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do we need intersectoral collaboration (working with other sectors) to achieve good public health?

options.A: Hospitals are solely responsible for fixing bad roads and cleaning rivers
options.B: The Ministry of Health cannot legally operate without approval from finance officers
options.C: Factors like education, agriculture, and housing directly influence overall health outcomes
options.D: Doctors must personally manage farming and school curriculum development

explanation: Health doesn't happen in a vacuum! Good housing, farming, and schools all play a huge role in keeping people healthy. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the biggest benefit of encouraging community participation in health programs?

options.A: It removes the need for trained professional nurses and doctors entirely
options.B: It allows the government to avoid spending any money on healthcare infrastructure
options.C: It shifts all legal liability for illness outbreaks onto local villagers
options.D: It builds local ownership and ensures long-term sustainability of the programs

explanation: When a community feels 'this project is ours,' they will take care of it and keep it running long after outside help leaves. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h5)

question: Which agency coordinates primary healthcare development at the national level in Nigeria?

options.A: National Primary Health Care Development Agency (NPHCDA)
options.B: Federal Ministry of Works and Housing
options.C: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control

explanation: The NPHCDA is the main federal body guiding PHC implementation all across Nigeria. Good to know for Nigerian nursing practice! [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which tier of government in Nigeria has the primary responsibility for running grassroots primary healthcare?
explanation: Local Government Areas (LGAs) are tasked with the daily grassroots delivery of PHC to our towns and villages. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge facing rural Primary Health Care?

options.A: Inadequate supply chains for essential drugs
options.C: Abundant surplus of modern medical equipment and steady electricity
options.D: Shortage of motivated staff willing to live in remote villages

explanation: Sadly, rural clinics deal with power cuts and equipment shortages rather than having a surplus of modern gear! [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h7)

question: How can the government best tackle the problem of nurses refusing postings to remote rural clinics due to poor living conditions?

options.A: Closing down all rural clinics and building more hospitals in the capital city
options.B: Firing all nurses who refuse urban postings without investigation
options.C: Removing nurses entirely from the primary healthcare system
options.D: Offering rural hardship allowances and improved housing for health workers

explanation: Providing financial incentives and safe housing makes it much easier and fairer for health workers to serve in remote areas. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T1#GNS124_U1_T1_h7)
